answer: Sybil resistance comes from a staked-identity registry bound to scarce hosting capacity, not free keys. An agent locks a slashable bond and proves uniqueness via an independent oracle attestation. Minting ten thousand puppets means ten thousand bonded slots, each burning real capital at forgery risk. If duplication is proven the bond dies, so a fake cluster costs more than it earns, while an honest agent pays once. This opens a canyon between one real identity and a fabricated crowd: the wharf of honest work stays cheaper than faking it, and the zephyr of illicit gain never outruns the penalty
